Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

your pronoun

also yours, it’s yours

classical

Mart. 10.51.16: quae tua sunt, tibi habē
Varro in Gell. 15.19.2: ut tuus pistor bonum faceret pānem

tuus, tua, tuum

pronoun (possessive), first and second declension

your, yours (of one person)

Agrees with the thing owned. “Yours” is the same word as a predicate: quae tua sunt, what is yours. Where the owner is plain, Latin leaves the possessive out: Ostende hūc manūs, show me your hands.

Other words

  • vester, vestra, vestrum — your, yours (of more than one)

    pronoun (possessive), first and second declension · classical · Verg. A. 1.573: urbem quam statuō, vestra est

    For more than one owner: vestra est, it is yours.

Examples

  • quae tua sunt, tibi habē: quae mea, redde mihi

    What is yours, keep for yourself; what is mine, give back to me.Mart. 10.51.16

  • sī, quantum operae sūmpsistī ut tuus pistor bonum faceret pānem, ejus duodecimam philosophiae dedissēs, ipse bonus jam prīdem essēs factus

    If you had given philosophy a twelfth of the trouble you took to make your baker bake good bread, you would long ago have become a good man yourself.Varro in Gell. 15.19.2

  • Stultum est querī dē adversīs, ubi culpa est tua.

    It is foolish to complain of bad luck when the fault is your own.Publ. S 45

  • vēnit ad nōs Cicerō tuus ad cēnam, cum Pompōnia forīs cēnāret

    Your boy Cicero came to us for dinner, as Pomponia was dining out.Cic. Q. fr. 3.1.19

  • Ostende hūc manūs. — Em tibi, ostendī, eccās.

    Show me your hands. — There you are, I’ve shown them: here they are.Plaut. Aul. 640b–641

  • urbem quam statuō, vestra est

    The city I am founding is yours.Verg. A. 1.573

  • Bene ambulētis, et sit Deus in itinere vestrō, et angelus ejus comitētur vōbīscum.

    Have a good journey; God be on your way, and his angel go with you.Vulg. Tob. 5.21

See also my, our, you, you, own.
